mappings.mapping_rationale: KSA-01 lifecycle scope is the operational-versus-semantic state distinction enforced by durable checkpoint, retry, cancellation, and NEEDS_REVIEW behavior.

ksa_scope_registry.scope: canonical host-adapter contract and one normal employee workflow

mappings.mapping_rationale: KSA-02 requires the canonical host adapter to expose one normal employee workflow.
KSA-03 covers native OpenCode invocation through the employee workflow contract.
KSA-03 attachment and workspace intake must preserve immutable multi-file source boundaries.

ksa_scope_registry.scope: first-class Cloud VS Code adapter with current/selected files and host parity

mappings.mapping_rationale: KSA-04 is specifically a host-parity requirement; current/selected Cloud VS Code file intake remains an open repository scope.

ksa_scope_registry.future_project_os_owner: Project OS KSA-04 owner to deliver and reconcile the full queued host scope.

ksa_scope_registry.scope: Decision View, reconstruction, review disclosure and evidence drill-down parity across hosts

mappings.mapping_rationale: KSA-05 includes Decision View parity across hosts, which remains open with the queued Cloud VS Code host scope.
KSA-05 directly governs reconstructed Decision View, review disclosure, and evidence drill-down.

ksa_scope_registry.future_project_os_owner: Project OS KSA-05 owner to deliver and reconcile the full queued host scope.

mappings.mapping_rationale: KSA-06 directly specifies durable execution, job, checkpoint, and run-store behavior.
KSA-07 requires the pinned production runtime artifact and exact production model.
The deployed runtime and production model require candidate-bound company qualification evidence.
KSA-08 requires durable worker execution, checkpoints, retry, and cancellation.
A durable production PaaS worker/controller requires company deployment qualification.
KSA-09 directly governs scoped persistence, queueing, and concurrency.
Production persistence and concurrency isolation require deployment-bound company evidence.

ksa_scope_registry.scope: exact candidate/run identity and compatible resume

mappings.mapping_rationale: KSA-10 requires exact run, runtime, model, OCR, and terminology identity on compatible resume.
The deployed runtime and model identity require production-bound qualification.
KSA-11 directly governs the three-class storage model.

ksa_scope_registry.scope: separate content and operational-metadata retention with no authoritative 30-day default

mappings.mapping_rationale: KSA-12 directly governs separate content and operational-metadata retention policies.
KSA-13 directly governs deletion, expiry, and legal-hold behavior.
KSA-14 directly governs runtime AccessKey consumption and fail-closed authentication.
Company production authentication authority must be verified against the deployed candidate.
KSA-15 directly governs prevention of AccessKey leakage from persisted and source-bearing data.
KSA-16 directly governs authoritative classification admission.
Deployed classification authority and data-use routing require company qualification evidence.
KSA-17 directly governs run-scoped authorization and tenant isolation.
Production tenant and IAM isolation require candidate-bound company evidence.
KSA-18 directly governs default-deny production egress.
Production network policy and egress authority require company qualification evidence.
KSA-19 directly governs governed company termbase resolution.
The deployed company termbase authority and identity require candidate-bound qualification.
KSA-20 directly governs controlled content-bearing diagnostic support.
Production support access authority and data-use controls require company qualification evidence.
KSA-21 directly governs adversarial document and prompt-injection security.
Production security qualification must verify the deployed candidate against adversarial input risk.
KSA-22 directly governs source facts, supported interpretation, and unresolved provenance.
KSA-23 directly governs conflict and supersession objects.
KSA-24 directly governs mixed-language, table, chart, diagram, and modality fidelity.
KSA-25 directly governs unreadable, decorative, and cross-document recovery states.
KSA-26 directly governs four-set corpus taxonomy and contamination controls.
KSA-27 directly governs non-compensable hard gates and policy floors.
KSA-28 directly governs repetition, stability, and false-DONE calibration.
KSA-29 directly governs bilingual gold and adjudication workflow.
Production use of bilingual gold and adjudication requires candidate-bound data-use and evaluator qualification.
KSA-30 directly governs the zero-Korean employee-study protocol.
Human-study outcomes and employee data-use evidence must be supplied and reviewed outside the repository.
KSA-31 directly governs champion promotion and scoped recertification/invalidation.
A production champion decision requires externally qualified evidence and governance.
KSA-32 directly governs protected release governance.
Live protected-branch and release authority require company-owned evidence.
KSA-32 release evidence must be bound to the exact candidate and its open blockers.
KSA-32 release governance remains distinct from production certification.
KSA-33 directly governs candidate-bound security release evidence.
Current company security and deployment evidence must be bound to the candidate.
KSA-33 security results must be tied to the exact candidate and qualification record.
KSA-33 repository evidence does not establish production certification.
KSA-34 directly governs cohort, pilot, canary, and reversible rollout controls.
Pilot, canary, and rollout outcomes require company-owned candidate evidence.
KSA-34 rollout blockers and evidence must be bound to the exact candidate.
KSA-34 rollout controls do not by themselves establish production certification.
KSA-35 directly governs non-content telemetry and employee issue reporting.
Live telemetry and employee reporting governance require company qualification.
KSA-35 evidence and open reporting blockers must be bound to the exact candidate.
KSA-35 telemetry evidence is distinct from production certification.
KSA-36 directly governs performance/load measurement and resource budgets.
Production load and company capacity require measured candidate-bound evidence.
KSA-36 measurements and unresolved budgets must be bound to the exact candidate.
KSA-36 performance results do not substitute for production certification.
KSA-37 directly governs candidate revocation, kill-switch, and drift response.
Company deployment authority must qualify the production revocation and recovery path.
KSA-37 revocation and drift evidence must be bound to the exact candidate.
KSA-37 revocation qualification remains separate from production certification.
